bet.text: Two separately controlled turrets that shoot on the move, so if one jams the other is ready.

auto.text: At the St. Louis Regional: start at the trench at about a 90 degree angle, go straight into the pile, return over the bump, shoot on the move to the other trench, collect another load, cross the bump again, then depot or climb. The robot could climb and shoot together.

cycle.text: The full-width intake fills a hopper that the intake's extension enlarges. Cones push balls through the spindexer onto two ramps, one to each shooter. Each turret aims on its own and shoots on the move; near its turning limit it decides whether to keep turning or flip around.

endgame.text: At the St. Louis Regional the robot had an L1 climber.

fallback.text: The turrets run separately, so if one jams the other still shoots.

gave_up.text: The St. Louis version climbed only to L1. The team says it saved weight, seemed to work better for auto and was much quicker than flipping upside down.

changed.text: The spindexer moved from bristle brushes, which jammed, to stacked wheels, then to a cone, later ribbed, to raise the feed rate.

Replies that read as the team's say the championship CAD keeps a tube that is a remnant of the climber, and that a sloped plate after the intake reduced jamming as the intake pulled in, after a few iterations.

outcome.text: 45-2-0 in official play; finalist in the Hopper division; ranked 11 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 314.96, Hopper).

facts.text: A reply that reads as the team's says the narrow modules let the team put their bulk where it wanted and keep the spindexer as large as possible

solves.text: Pick up balls at any robot speed without pushing them away or jamming

facts.text: Two Kraken X60s: one for pitch, one for the rollers
Four silicone-wrapped rollers: three carbon fiber, one polycarbonate
Roller voltage rises linearly with chassis speed, from about 6.5 V to a maximum of about 12 V
A reply that reads as the team's says the intake plates clip the bumper slightly, pushing into its foam to keep a good hole-to-edge distance

solves.text: Hold more fuel with few moving parts

facts.text: The intake's extension expands the hopper, so there are fewer moving parts
SRPP walls and an expandable net on the roof instead of a rising roof
The intake can jump up and down to hold more balls and agitate them

solves.text: Feed two turrets from one hopper without jams

facts.text: Ribbed cones agitate, pull balls down and push them into the shooter; cone, floor and gearbox are one system on an X44
A taped SRPP disc drives balls against an outer polycarbonate rim, with two ramps, one into each shooter
A more extreme cone made balls bounce too much; a smaller, rounder cone put too little energy into them
A reply that reads as the team's says a plate sloped up out of the intake reduces jamming as the intake pulls in

cost.text: It was changed several times: bristle brushes jammed and let balls keep circling, and stacked wheels of about 4, 3 and 2 in were less effective

solves.text: Track the hub on the move with either turret

facts.text: Rotation in each direction before a turret must flip all the way around, about
At about 190 degrees an algorithm decides whether to keep turning or flip around
The energy chain runs down, up and down to the front of the robot; polycarbonate panels protect the wiring at the front
A reply that reads as the team's says each turret has two CANcoders, combined with the Chinese remainder theorem for accurate position
A reply that reads as the team's says everything on a shooter had to fit a 12 in diameter cylinder, a strict design constraint

solves.text: Shoot at the hub while moving, and over its own hopper

facts.text: Aluminum flywheels, size about
An X60 drives the shooter and an X44 drives the rack for its vertical angle
Hood travel is about 10 to 45 degrees
Each turret has a front and a back kicker wheel
A reply that reads as the team's says the front wheel and the rear accelerator wheels run at different speeds

functions.name: Moving-shot code and localization

solves.text: Aim two turrets while the robot moves

functions.type: vector aiming with odometry and Limelight 4

facts.text: Vectors from hub to robot center and then to each turret give distance; a linear interpolation table gives voltage, power and angle
Each turret runs its own command
Three Limelight 4 cameras and swerve odometry estimate pose; MegaTag2 is trusted only in very good conditions

functions.name: Undermounted battery and electronics

solves.text: Package the battery around the spindexers and shooters

functions.type: battery and electronics below the robot

facts.text: A machined plate with four pins holds the battery; popping one pin on each side releases the panel
Electronics are also underneath, clear of other mechanisms and with straight wire runs

decisions.because: if one jams, the other is still ready
it saves weight, seems to work better for auto and is much quicker than flipping upside down (St. Louis version)
decisions.instead_of: a climb that flips upside down

decisions.because: it kept more constant contact and raised the feed rate
it expands capacity without a rising roof
packaging was very difficult around the spindexers and shooters; the team says batteries never fall out or move
